title: Palimpsest China Censorship Analysis
description: Current cross-instrument analysis of China's information controls with sentence-level evidence receipts.

items.title: China censorship today: network layer elevated in the latest board synthesis
items.summary: 10 of 10 selected censorship instruments are current. The evidence spans attention, silence, network interference, erasure, and app distribution, but their denominators remain separate.
items.content_text:
China's information controls must be read as separate content, network, erasure, and distribution measurements rather than one seductive national score.

The board detects movement, not motive

Upstream board reports: single layer elevated: network. 33 of 33 configured sources report; 32 are live. Health qualifiers: 1 degraded. The board-wide e-value is 25.929; the predeclared board alarm threshold is 20. The board statistic tests whether named signals moved beyond their own histories; it does not identify one cause for the movement. The current coverage audit marks 1 signal as confounded by its measurement coverage.

Attention, silence, and erasure answer different questions

The current deletion-directive index ranks 207 terms with documented censorship provenance. 0 blackout topics meet the predeclared rule among 25 topics considered in this round. The current cross-layer erasure index is 39.9. The directive index counts provenance-bound terms, the silence index tests a predeclared blackout rule, and the erasure index summarizes heterogeneous layers; placing them together does not create one censorship rate.

Network measurements agree on scope, not on one denominator

The current coverage-weighted fusion of reporting vantages is 28.9%. The current OONI aggregate reports a 58.8% anomaly index across 274,022 completed China measurements. The current controlled panel reports 100% blocked responses across 4 tested domains. The fused index, volunteer-probe aggregate, and fixed inside-China panel use different samples and protocols, so none can be substituted for a national share of traffic or users.

App availability needs both a fixed panel and a broad corpus

The current panel finds 60% of 10 tracked apps unavailable in the China storefront. The current AppleCensorship corpus reports 28.15% unavailable among 109,308 tested apps for mainland China. The fixed panel supports controlled same-round comparison, while the broad corpus improves catalogue coverage; neither percentage identifies why an individual app is absent.

What today's reading can support

At the edition clock, 10 of 10 selected instruments publish current claims and 0 publish availability warnings instead. The defensible conclusion is a layered description of current observations, not a single estimate of censorship prevalence or intent.
